chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassa' from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) fasted until it was said, 'He will not break his fast.' Then he broke his fast until it was said, 'He will not fast.' Then he fasted the fast of Dawud (peace be upon him), one day and one day not. Then he passed away while fasting three days in the month. He said: 'Indeed, these equate to the fasting of the whole month, and they remove the 'wahr' of the chest, and the 'wahr' is the anxiety.'

Hammad said: 'So I said, 'And which days are these?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The first Thursday of the month, and the first Wednesday after the tenth of it, and the last Thursday in it.' So I said, 'How did these days become the ones in which is to be fasted?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, those before us from the nations, whenever punishment descended upon any one of them, it descended during these days. Thus, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) fasted these fearful days.'

key_terms.الْمَخُوفَةَ: The fearful days, referring to days historically associated with divine punishment.
key_terms.صَوْمَ دَاوُدَ: The fast of Dawud (David), a practice of fasting one day and skipping one day alternately.
key_terms.وَحَرِ الصَّدْرِ: Anxiety or restlessness of the chest/heart.

ai.seo_question: What are the specific three days of the month that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) fasted to emulate the fast of Dawud and avoid divine punishment?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s transition to the *Sawm Dawud* (fast of David), a highly revered alternating fast, while also prescribing three specific monthly days to ward off divine affliction (*Wahar*), understood in Shia tradition as spiritual whispers or calamities. The scholarly context emphasizes the prophetic wisdom of aligning human worship with cosmic rhythms, as these specific days were historically associated with the descent of punishment upon previous nations, making them opportune times for intercession and protection.
